The browser displays the effect's number and name as recorded in the 2DA file.  For many effects, such as VFX_DUR_BLUR, the name matches the constant defined for scripting.  However for others the name and constant differ; or the constant is defined in an include file; or there is no constant.  In all cases there is a simple solution: use the effect number instead.

The browser displays the effect's number and name as recorded in the 2DA file.  While the name helps us humans identify an effect, the number is all-important.  Often called the "magic number" you can use this number to generate an effect even if you don't know its VFX_* or AOE_* constant.

Yes.  From the main menu select "Browse effects" then either "Area of effect" or "Visual effect" then Keyword and finally "User-defined". You can now speak the effect's name or name fragment aloud and when you have completed the conversation you can click the Browser's Next or Previous.  You may find your name or name fragment produces multiple matches.  For example "nature" will produce four matches.

Yes.  From the main menu select "Browse effects" then either "Area of effect" or "Visual effect" and finally "Number".  You can now speak the effect's magic number aloud and when you have completed the conversation you can click the Browser's Next or Previous

Yes and no.  There is no "Browse All" function however you will achieve almost the same thing if you view both AOE shapes and all four VFX types.  Also some effects, for example 508 - VFX_DUR_UNSUPPORTED_CAGE, cause problems for the browser and cannot be displayed.

Forcing a full cache will read all relevant data into memory.  This should improve the browser performance by minimising delays between effects when first encountered.  

NOTE: your system will hang for several (10-20) seconds while the data is read and stored.
